kubernetes.description: The kubernetes manager ships with no file patterns of its own, so without this it reads nothing. The cluster's own manifests pin gatus, valkey, stalwart and busybox by tag.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A security fix skips the cooldown, so it never merges itself: a release that has not aged gets a person instead.

customManagers.description: The Brevo and Discord clients publish only to GitHub Packages, which needs a registry token Renovate does not have, so a maven lookup returns no-result. Follow the source repositories' release tags instead.

packageRules.description: No rule here sets a groupName, so every dependency gets its own pull request and a young or failing one holds back nothing else. The only sets left are the ones Renovate builds itself: a monorepo's packages and a shared Gradle version variable, which break when they move apart.
Every action is pinned to a commit digest here, so Renovate keeps the digest and the version comment in step.
A major bump needs code changes. Dashboard approval keeps it out of the queue until someone picks it up, and the automerge rule below leaves it out.

Anything short of a major merges itself once every required check passes. Lock file maintenance stays out: it pulls transitive releases that have not waited out the cooldown. The cluster rule below turns this back off for the Flux tree.

build.yml publishes the production images and release.yml cuts the release, both with credentials, and no pull request check runs either workflow. An action used there would merge on age alone, so it gets a reviewed pull request.
A cluster chart or controller image reaches production the moment it merges, so each one gets a reviewed pull request and never merges itself.
gotk-components.yaml is regenerated as a whole by the flux manager. Bumping its controller images through the kubernetes manager would leave Flux half upgraded.
The site's own images are pinned by digest, written by the release pipeline, not by a pull request.

net.blueshell.clients resolves only from GitHub Packages, which needs a registry token Renovate does not have. The custom managers above follow the source repositories' tags instead, so the maven lookup is off to keep no-result entries off the dashboard.
The clients are ours, and they already hold their own dependencies for the cooldown period. A release of theirs carries an API change the site needs at once, so it waits for nothing.
CI, dev compose and the changeset render run production's MariaDB, 10.11.10, pinned in platform/cluster/flux/apps/data/mariadb/release.yaml. A bump there comes first (#1738); these follow it by hand.
